headline: ChatGPT's Work-with-Apps reads what's on screen while Claude Code executes — high data-leakage risk via screen+terminal coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pasting Claude Code terminal output into ChatGPT (or letting Work-with-Apps read it) ingests untrusted strings from web/MCP results into ChatGPT's context. Similarly, copying ChatGPT output back into Claude Code can re-inject instructions. Bridge is manual paste plus Work-with-Apps screen reading.
mitigations: Disable ChatGPT Work-with-Apps when Claude Code is running secrets-touching commands
Read pasted ChatGPT output critically before letting Claude Code execute it

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT desktop captures screenshots and (with Work-with-Apps) reads from Terminal and IDEs, which can include any file Claude Code has open or any repo path on screen. ChatGPT uses inputs for training unless the user opts out. Two separate vendors see code via two different channels.
mitigations: Opt out of ChatGPT model training in Data Controls
Revoke ChatGPT Accessibility/Screen Recording permissions when not needed
Avoid using ChatGPT desktop on machines holding regulated data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT desktop cannot write to the filesystem or commit to git, so it cannot conflict with Claude Code's writes. Surface is limited to clipboard.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plausible: ChatGPT proposes a fix the user pastes verbatim into Claude Code, which executes it without re-derivation. No verification handshake between the tools.
mitigations: Re-derive answers in Claude Code rather than executing pasted suggestions blind

E_compliance.rationale: Different processors with different training/retention policies handle the same source code. For regulated data this is a documented finding; ChatGPT default is opted-in to training.
mitigations: Use ChatGPT Enterprise for stronger data-handling commitments
